message.content:
You're building live SEO landing pages for 5 new games on Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript, staging tree at /opt/nxeon-staging — work only in staging, never /opt/nxeon prod tree. Never run `npm run build`; verify only with `npx tsc --noEmit`).

Context: earlier today, 5 new games were scaffolded at the DATA LAYER ONLY (non-provisioning): Dragonwilds, Abiotic Factor, Core Keeper, Icarus, Sunkenland. Find this scaffolding — search `lib/games.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`, `lib/game-config.ts` and any other `lib/game-*.ts` files for these 5 names (case-insensitive grep) to see exactly what's already defined: display names, slugs, ports, hero-art asset keys, whatever fields exist. This is the "growth" reasoning: Nxeon added new games verified to have real, beatable search demand (per an earlier SEO research pass) — the plan was always to build real landing pages for organic search, but actual server-provisioning support for these games might be a separate, not-yet-built piece. You need to determine, precisely, from the code: is a customer able to actually check out and deploy one of these 5 games today (i.e. does the deploy wizard / game-selection UI already list them as purchasable), or is the data scaffolding purely groundwork with no real purchase path yet?

Also check `public/games/art/` for whether hero/poster/logo art assets already exist for these 5 games (e.g. `dragonwilds_hero.jpg`, `abiotic-factor_hero.jpg`, etc. — check the actual slug naming convention used in `lib/games.ts` for these entries) — if art is missing, you cannot build a good page (do not use a placeholder from an unrelated game — that exact mismatch bug was just found and fixed on the mods page today, don't reintroduce it elsewhere).

There is an existing individual-game landing page template used for already-live games — find an existing single-game live landing page (e.g. search `app/(marketing)/` for an existing route like `palworld-server-hosting` or `valheim-server-hosting` — check `next.config.ts` or `app/sitemap.ts` for the exact list of existing live "[game]-server-hosting" paths) and read one as your pattern/reference (both the page.tsx and whatever shared component it renders — there's likely a shared single-game-landing component used across all of these, find it).

Your job:
1. Determine real purchasability for each of the 5 games (report this either way, don't guess).
2. Determine art asset availability for each of the 5 games.
3. For any game that HAS both (a) real art assets and (b) is genuinely purchasable/orderable today (even if provisioning isn't fully automated — e.g. if it's manual/beta-flagged, that's fine, just be accurate about what CTA to show), build a real live page at the same URL convention as the existing games (e.g. `/dragonwilds-server-hosting`), using the existing shared single-game-landing pattern/component (not a new one-off — reuse infrastructure), with correct metadata, JSON-LD, and add the route to `app/sitemap.ts`'s static routes list (matching the existing entries' pattern) and to any relevant nav/game-directory listing component so it's actually discoverable/linked from the site (an orphan page with no internal links is much weaker for SEO — check how existing game pages are linked from `/game-servers` or similar hub pages and add these 5 the same way).
4. For any game that's missing art assets or isn't actually purchasable yet, do NOT build a live page for it — building a page with a broken "Deploy" flow or placeholder art is worse than not having the page. Instead, clearly report which games are blocked and on what (missing art vs missing purchase path vs both).
5. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm clean.

Report back (under 350 words): a clear per-game status (built-live / blocked-on-X), what routes you created, whether they're linked from the game-servers hub and in the sitemap, and tsc status. If zero games ended up buildable, say so plainly and explain the blocker rather than forcing something broken live.

However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text: All 19 already-live games have GamePlan tiers and existing landing pages — the 5 new games (Dragonwilds, Sunkenland, Abiotic Factor, Core Keeper, Icarus) have none of that. This fully confirms the finding without needing to build anything. No page should be built for any of them today.

`npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (no changes were made, since no game qualified for a live page).

## Findings

**Data-layer scaffolding found** in `lib/games.ts` (the single source of truth others import from — `lib/game-config.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts` etc. all derive from it): all 5 games (`dragonwilds`, `sunkenland`, `abioticfactor`, `corekeeper`, `icarus`) have `GAME_FAMILIES` entries, `GAME_DISPLAY` names/glyphs, `GAME_PORT` guesses, and `GAME_ART_SLUG` placeholder keys. The code's own comments are explicit and match what I independently verified: `lib/games.ts:40-41` says **"SCAFFOLD ONLY 2026-08-31, NOT yet orderable — no GamePlan/OsTemplate seeded"**, and `lib/games.ts:140-143` says **"art not yet produced"**.

**1. Purchasability — none of the 5 are orderable today.**
`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:210-211` builds the wizard's game list as `GAME_FAMILIES.filter(f => withTiers.has(f))`, where `withTiers` comes from seeded `GamePlan` pricing tiers. I grepped `prisma/` (`seed-wave1-games.ts`, `seed-wave2-games.ts`, `seed-gameplans.ts`, `catalog.ts`, etc.) — zero references to any of the 5 games. No GamePlan tiers, no OsTemplate rows. They will never appear in the deploy wizard or checkout regardless of what `lib/games.ts` defines. There is no purchase path, manual or automated.

**2. Art assets — none exist.**
`ls public/games/art/ | grep -i` for all 5 slugs returned nothing. `GAME_ART_SLUG` currently points `hero` at the bare family key as an explicit placeholder (same pattern used for `minecraft`'s missing poster), with a comment saying real art "drops in before launch." No hero/poster/logo files exist for any of the 5.

**3. Result: all 5 blocked on both purchasability AND art.** Per the task's own instructions, this is exactly the "do NOT build" case — no game has real art + real purchase path, so I built nothing.

**Actions taken:** none. No routes created, no sitemap changes, no hub/nav changes, no new files. This was a verification-only pass — building any of these pages now would ship dead "Deploy" CTAs and reused/missing art, the same class of bug called out from the mods-page incident.

`npx tsc --noEmit`: clean, no errors (expected, since no code was changed).

**Recommendation:** this is now a blocked/owner-decision item — needs (a) GamePlan/OsTemplate seeding + a provisioning story (even manual/beta) for at least one of the 5, and (b) real key art per game, before any landing page work is worth doing. Worth logging to the Nxeon roadmap/memory rather than retrying later without those two things in place.
